summary: Set up centralized log forwarding from node2's inventory application to node1 using rsyslog over TCP, persisted the received logs to /var/log/inventory/node2.log, and verified the flow survives independent restarts of both nodes.
actions_performed: Investigated node2 and found no pre-existing 'inventory' app; created /usr/local/bin/inventory-app.sh (logs heartbeat messages via `logger -t inventory` every 5s) and a systemd unit /etc/systemd/system/inventory.service (Restart=always, enabled at boot) to simulate the application generating log traffic.

On node1: created /var/log/inventory (owned syslog:syslog, mode 775 so rsyslogd can write) and /etc/rsyslog.d/60-inventory-receive.conf loading imtcp, listening on port 10514, and writing all received messages to /var/log/inventory/node2.log via a dedicated ruleset.

On node2: created /etc/rsyslog.d/60-inventory-forward.conf forwarding messages with programname 'inventory' to node1 (10.100.18.10:10514) via omfwd/TCP with an infinite retry count and a disk-assisted queue (queue.saveOnShutdown=on) so buffered messages survive network/process interruptions.
Verified rsyslog config validity (rsyslogd -N1) on both nodes before restarting rsyslog to apply it; confirmed TCP listener on node1 and confirmed messages appearing in /var/log/inventory/node2.log.
Diagnosed and fixed an omfile write failure caused by directory ownership/permissions (root:root 755) blocking the syslog user from creating the log file.
Captured healthy baseline (boot_id, service active/enabled state, live log tail) on both nodes.

Restarted node1 via `systemctl reboot`, polled until exec was available again, confirmed a changed boot_id, confirmed rsyslog auto-started and the TCP listener reappeared, and confirmed new inventory messages continued arriving from node2 with no manual intervention.

Restarted node2 via `systemctl reboot` (only after node1 had fully recovered, restarting one node at a time), polled until exec was available again, confirmed a changed boot_id, confirmed rsyslog and inventory.service auto-started (both enabled+active), and confirmed the forwarded log stream resumed on node1 with a fresh sequence of heartbeat messages.

evidence.requirement: inventory application log messages forwarded from node2 to a centralized collector on node1
evidence.summary: inventory.service on node2 emits via logger -t inventory; node2 rsyslog forwards programname=inventory messages via omfwd/TCP to node1:10514; node1's ruleset writes them to /var/log/inventory/node2.log, confirmed by tailed heartbeat entries seq=11,12.

evidence.requirement: received messages persisted on node1 under /var/log/inventory/node2.log
evidence.summary: Created /etc/rsyslog.d/60-inventory-receive.conf targeting /var/log/inventory/node2.log, fixed directory permissions, and confirmed the file exists with real content.

evidence.requirement: healthy baseline captured before any restart
evidence.summary: Captured node1 boot_id e8afb731..., rsyslog active/enabled, and existing log content; captured node2 boot_id a0c36ad2..., rsyslog and inventory.service active/enabled.

evidence.requirement: node1 restarted one at a time with changed boot identity proven and recovery verified
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; node1 unreachable during reboot; came back with new boot_id a3dcf461... (was e8afb731...); rsyslog active with TCP listener restored; new inventory messages (seq 17,18,19) continued arriving live, proving recovery.

evidence.requirement: node2 restarted one at a time (after node1 fully recovered) with changed boot identity proven and recovery verified
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acknowledged before disconnect; node2 unreachable during reboot; came back with new boot_id 9e8b1a6e... (was a0c36ad2...); rsyslog and inventory.service both auto-started (active+enabled) with no manual intervention; node1's log file resumed receiving fresh heartbeat messages (new seq 1,2,3) confirming full end-to-end recovery.
